newsitem.title: USA: Tribune reports profit rise, Times posts a loss.
newsitem.headline: Tribune reports profit rise, Times posts a loss.

text.p: Tribune Co. announced an 18 perecent gain in third-quarter profits to $66 million Friday, while The New York Times Co. posted a $47.7 million loss, mainly due to an accounting change.
Excluding the charge, the Times reported a strong rise in profits. Both companies cited gains in publishing and broadcasting for the improvement.

Tribune, which owns the Chicago Tribune, television and radio outlets and the Chicago Cubs baseball team, said its earnings amounted to $1 a share, up from $56 million, or 79 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter.
Sales grew 12 percent to $618 million from $552 million.
Tribune stock rose $1.50 to $82.625 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Broadcasting and entertainment operating profit rose 18 percent, due mainly to improvements at the Cubs and in the radio group, the company said. Tribune agreed in July to acquire Renaissance Communications Corp., which owns six television stations.
Tribune said operating profit in its publishing operations jumped 17 percent, due to gains from all newspapers.
Tribune's education group reported operating profit of $22 million compared with $3 million in 1995, due to contributions from recent acquisitions.

"These results reflect a different Tribune," Chairman John Madigan said. "We've changed dramatically in recent years. We're making a major move in broadcasting with the pending acquisition of Renaissance, and we're developing a very exciting education business that is not dependent on advertising."
Advertising revenues increased 6 percent, while newsprint and ink expense fell 14 percent, as average newsprint prices fell 10 percent.

Tribune owns and operates 10 television and five radio stations, publishes four daily newspapers, produces and syndicates programming and information, and provides educational products and services for schools and consumers.

The Times Co., which publishes The New York Times, said the $47.7 million loss for the quarter amounted to 49 cents a share, compared with net income of $32.2 million, or 33 cents a share in the year-ago quarter.
The company also also publishes The Boston Globe, 21 regional newspapers and nine magazines, and operates eight television stations and two New York City radio stations.

Excluding the accounting charge and one time items in both years, the company said its third-quarter earnings would have $37.4 million, or 38 cents per share, compared with $27.2 million, or 28 cents per share.

Revenues rose 9.8 percent to $629 million from $573 million a year ago, the company said, citing improved newspaper and broadcast operations and higher earnings from paper mills in which the company has investments.

"The company's strong operating results demonstrate our success in obtaining premium prices for our premium-quality newspapers, and strong performance from our broadcast properties," Times Chairman Arthur Ochs Sulzberger said in a statement.

Company President Russell Lewis pointed to higher advertising and circulation revenues for newspapers and increased revenues and profits from two newly acquired NBC-affiliated TV stations, which benefited from the network's coverage of the Summer Olympics.
"We are continuing to focus on controlling our operating costs so that we can further increase margins," Lewis said.
The company's stock slipped 62.5 cents to $35.125 on the American Stock Exchange.

The Times Co.'s newspapers, which account for 89 percent of its revenues, saw operating profit rise to $62.7 million from $36.1 million in 1995's third quarter, excluding the accounting charge and the cost of employee buyouts.

Operating profit from its magazines, which contribute 7 percent of revenue, declined slightly to $7.4 million from $7.5 million, excluding the accounting charge. Its broadcast properties' operating profit rose to $7.3 million from $4.4 million, excluding buyouts.
